weakness: The program had exactly one way to make contact with the knob (a top-down pinch at a fixed yaw). A tall box standing 6 cm beside the knob, inside the ~20 cm footprint of the hand along its closing axis, made the planner refuse that approach on every seed. The program also did not notice the refusal: the gripper was still open (width 0.08), only a fully closed gripper counted as a miss, so it went on to 'twist' empty air about a stale axis and retried the same refused grasp three times.
how_found: Questioned A6 (nothing is beside the fin within the hand's footprint). Stove knobs on real counters sit next to bottles, pans and spice jars, and the pinch needs room for the whole hand body, not just the fingertips, so clutter near the knob was the most likely real-world violation.
why_missed: In the nominal scene the knob area was empty, so the first strategy worked on 10/10 seeds and I never checked what grasp() returns when the approach is refused, nor how much space the hand body needs compared with the part it grasps.
fix: (1) Treat a refused/incomplete approach or a gripper that is still fully open as a failed pinch. (2) Own pinch routine that tries a top-down approach and hand rolls of +-0.35/0.6 rad about the fin axis. (3) If no pinch is feasible, find movable objects whose box comes within 13 cm of the knob and relocate them: top grasp first, then side grasp, then push them away with closed fingers; set them down 15 cm further from the knob in the first direction the planner accepts. (4) Kept a tangential fingertip push of the fin as a last resort (weak in practice). Tried and rejected: pushing the fin tangentially (lever arm too short for the heavy damped knob) and tilted pinches alone (hand body still hits the box).
general_rule: Check every primitive's outcome (refused, incomplete, or a gripper that did not close) before acting on it, and when the workspace around a target is cluttered, plan for the space the whole hand needs and clear movable clutter before falling back to weaker contact strategies.

weakness: Every contact strategy assumed free space above the part: the pinch came from (nearly) straight above and the wrist twist swings the whole hand about the knob axis. With a fixed shelf 12 cm above the knob, top-down pinches are refused; steeply pitched pinches reach the fin but every twist step is refused or force-limited by the shelf. The clutter routine also wasted its time trying to grasp and push the fixed shelf (gripper_holding is true on a fixed object).
how_found: Questioned A5/A16 (free space above the knob). Stove knobs often sit under range hoods, wall cabinets or pot handles, and the hand plus wrist need ~20 cm of vertical room for a top-down pinch.
why_missed: The nominal scene has open space above the knob, and I had only checked that the target pose of the pinch was feasible, not the room needed for the motion that follows it (the twist).
fix: Six repair iterations, not enough: (1) pinch orientations enumerated over pitch/roll and two approach distances, capped at 4 moving candidates; (2) a new fallback that pushes the tall end of the fin tangentially with closed fingertips from a near-horizontal hand, along the approach axis, re-seating from a fresh detection whenever the knob stops following; (3) twist and push loops stop after repeated refusal/no progress to save the 150 s step budget; (4) clutter excludes objects hanging above the knob. Push alone turns the knob on 7/10 seeds, but in the full pipeline seat attempts that move to a pre-pose and are then refused burn the step budget (6/10 StepLimitExceeded). Variation marked unsolved and reverted; the general improvements are kept (base 1.0, v1 1.0).
general_rule: Check feasibility of the whole manipulation (approach, the actuating motion and the retreat) in the actual free space before committing to a contact, and budget time: try cheap-to-refuse options first, cap expensive retries, and keep a non-grasping strategy (push or nudge) that needs less clearance.
